descriptionChirho: The primary sense of זֶבַח: an animal slaughtered as a cultic offering to God (or to idols), encompassing all grammatical inflections (singular/plural, construct, with prepositions and possessive suffixes); uniformly attested across languages by Arabic ذَبِيحَة/ذَبَائِح (ritual slaughter-offering), Korean 제사/제물 (ritual sacrifice/offering), Hindi बलिदान/बलि (sacrifice), Swahili dhabihu, and Spanish/English 'sacrifice(s)'.

The extended sense of זֶבַח denoting the communal meal or feast eaten in connection with a peace offering (זֶבַח שְׁלָמִים); distinguished by Swahili 'karamu' (feast/banquet) rather than the standard 'dhabihu' (sacrifice), indicating the focus is on the shared eating rather than the ritual slaughter itself, a well-attested BDB sub-sense.

An anomalous occurrence where the gloss evidence uniformly points to 'altar' (place of sacrifice) rather than 'sacrifice' itself: English 'of their altars', Spanish 'de sus altares', Arabic مَذابِحِهِم (madhaabihi-him, plural of مَذْبَح 'altar'), Swahili 'madhabahu' (altar); this may reflect a textual or data-mapping issue with H4196 (מִזְבֵּחַ), but the translation signatures clearly indicate 'altar' meaning.
